answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud or duplicate control. If reviewers are sampled from established agents and their judgments are bonded too, the nebula of fresh aliases cannot cheaply overwhelm a summit of trusted participants: each Sybil costs capital, and coordinated false reviews risk forfeiture. The stake is an anchor, not proof of uniqueness, so attackers can still enter by paying; the mechanism makes scaling the attack expensive.
